subject: Post-call: FinCo eval plan & dataset format (next steps)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finco.com>
Cc: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: FinCo eval plan & dataset format (next steps)

Hi Alex — thanks again for the time earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Key takeaways from the call:
- Primary use case: customer support summarization + suggested reply generation for FinCo web/mobile chat.
- TPS/latency targets: 95 p50 < 300ms during peak, batchable during off-peak.
- Main risk: quality regressions on short-context banking Q&A (high cost if hallucinations).

Recommended models to include in the eval:
1) redwood-instruct-v2 (recommended baseline — optimized for instruction-following and latency)
2) meta-llama2-13b-8bit (cost/quality tradeoff; good for longer context)
3) vicuna-13b-v1.5 (open baseline we can run for comparison)

Benchmarks & assets I’ll run against:
- Redwood internal banking benchmark (shared link below)
- Your sample prompt set (attached as finco_eval_prompt_set.csv)

Ask / next steps for FinCo:
1) Please upload a 500–1,000 example dataset of representative support threads (anonymized). Preferred format: JSONL with fields: id, prompt, expected_response, label_type. I attached a template (finco_eval_template.jsonl).
2) Confirm whether we should score on Exact Match / BLEU / Human-rated relevance. For generated replies I recommend a combined scoring: automated label match + 5-point human rating for hallucination risk.
3) Any PII/PHI constraints? If so, we can provision a private eval in your VPC.

Timeline & process:
- Once we get the dataset + scoring rubric, Redwood will run the eval (3–5 business days). We’ll provide: per-model metrics, failure-case examples, and recommended prompts/quantization profile to meet latency targets.

Links & resources: 
- FinCo benchmark (read-only): https://drive.google.com/finco-eval-benchmarks
- Console eval docs: https://app.redwood.ai/docs/evals

I’ll loop in Nikhil and Dev to provision a run and confirm infra/permission details.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142

Attachments: finco_eval_prompt_set.csv (sample prompts), finco_eval_template.jsonl (JSONL schema template)

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sandra Lee <sandra.lee@fincorp.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 09:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: FinCo eval plan & dataset format (next steps)

Thanks Marissa — really helpful summary. A few quick clarifications: 

1) Dataset: We can share ~800 historical chat threads. We'll need to scrub account numbers and replace names with placeholders. Is that okay for your JSONL template?
2) Scoring: For reply generation we care most about correctness and hallucination rate. We don’t expect exact-match — would prefer a weighted score: 60% automated relevance (token overlap / embedding similarity) + 40% human label for hallucinations/incorrect facts.
3) Private eval: We have strict data handling rules for financial data. If you need raw logs, we will require a Private eval run in our VPC or a redacted dataset. What are the options and lead times?

Also can you confirm pricing for a one-off eval (approx size 800, 3 models)?

Appreciate it — Alex
Alex Johnson
Product Lead, AI Platforms | FinCo
alex.johnson@finco.com | (212) 555-0199

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 08:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Post-call: FinCo eval plan & dataset format (please provision)

Dev / Nikhil — forwarding the thread with FinCo. Can you please: 
- Provision a private eval run in us-east-1 (FinCo requests private handling).
- Create a temporary S3 ingestion bucket with restricted access for finco-evals-2026-06.
- Confirm expected turnaround and pricing for ~800 examples across 3 model variants (redwood-instruct-v2, llama2-13b-8bit, vicuna-13b).

Notes: If private VPC is not necessary, we can accept a redacted JSONL. Alex is waiting on the options.

Thanks — feel free to loop in infra if needed.

Marissa

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finco.com>
Cc: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: FinCo eval plan & dataset format (please provision)

Alex — quick update from infra side: 
- We can run a private eval in your VPC (us-east-1) via our Private Eval agent. Lead time: ~4 business days after we receive network access details and a signed data handling addendum.
- If you prefer to send a redacted JSONL to our secured S3, we’ll spin up a one-off eval job (3 business days).
- Pricing: one-off eval run for ~800 examples across 3 models is $2,500 (includes human-review sample of 50 cases). If you'd like a larger human annotation set we can provide a quote.

Dataset format reminder (attached template): JSONL lines with keys: id (string), prompt (string), expected_response (string, optional), label (gold label or class), metadata (stringified json is OK). For generated-response scoring we’ll compute: embedding-similarity, ROUGE-L, and flag hallucination heuristics; we’ll also include a human-rating UI for the 50 sampled cases.

Next steps for Alex: share preference for private VPC vs redacted upload and send the dataset or S3 access. We’ll also need PO or billing contact to finalize booking.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.ai
